title: Standard RFP Response Library (Security & Compliance) — Redwood Inference
author: Naomi Feldman
content:
## Purpose
This page is the canonical, **approved** answer library for common security & compliance prompts in RFPs, security questionnaires, and vendor intake forms. It is designed to:
- Reduce time-to-respond and prevent inconsistent answers across AEs/SEs/CSMs.
- Keep responses aligned to current product reality across **Hosted**, **Dedicated**, and **Private** deployments.
- Provide **evidence pointers** and escalation guidance (Security/GRC vs Legal vs Product).

**Audience:** Sales, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, and Security/GRC.

**Do not forward this Confluence page to customers.** Use the field-ready PDFs (Security FAQ v2 + one-pagers) and the formal evidence-sharing workflow.

---

## How to use this library
1) Identify the question category below (e.g., “Encryption at Rest”, “Audit Logging”, “SOC 2”).
2) Copy the **Base Answer** and then add the correct **deployment-mode variant** (Hosted / Dedicated / Private).
3) If the question asks for attachments (SOC 2 report, pen test, policies), follow **Evidence Requests** guidance.
4) If any “Route to Security/GRC/Legal” triggers apply, stop and route.

**Answer hygiene rules**
- Avoid absolute language (e.g., “always”, “never”, “guarantee”).
- Only claim what we do today; if asked about roadmap, use the approved “roadmap” phrasing.
- If a customer asks for contractual commitments (SLA, incident notification timelines, audit rights), route to **Legal**.

---

## Deployment modes: standard definitions (copy/paste)
Use this snippet when the questionnaire requires you to define offerings.

**Hosted (Redwood API):** Redwood operates the control plane and data plane in Redwood-managed cloud environments. Customers access via API/SDK.

**Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated):** Redwood operates dedicated, customer-isolated GPU capacity. Redwood manages the service; capacity and some operational controls are scoped to the customer’s dedicated pools.

**Private (Redwood Private):** Redwood provides a private deployment option (VPC and/or on-prem). The customer controls the surrounding network and (depending on configuration) certain infrastructure/security controls. Redwood’s responsibilities and the customer’s responsibilities are defined in the shared responsibility model for the specific deployment.

**Shared responsibility note (approved):** Security outcomes depend on both Redwood’s controls and customer configuration/operational practices, particularly for Private deployments.

---

## Routing guide (when to escalate)
**Route to Security Engineering (Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei) when:**
- The customer asks for deep technical details not covered in one-pagers (e.g., specific event schemas, agent-based telemetry, custom log sinks, private cluster topology).
- The customer requests exceptions (custom retention, custom cryptography requirements, bespoke SIEM integration support).

**Route to GRC / Compliance (Olga Petrov / Daniel Carter) when:**
- The customer requests SOC 2 report, bridge letter, ISO certificates, pen test reports/summaries, policies, or evidence of controls.
- The customer requests a security posture attestation letter, vendor management forms, or control mapping (NIST/ISO/CSA).

**Route to Legal (Michael Grant / Sofia Mendes) when:**
- Contractual commitments are requested: DPAs, audit rights, breach notification timelines, limitation of liability, indemnification, security addenda, subprocessor terms.
- The customer requests redlines to a security appendix or vendor terms.

**Route to Product (Nikhil Sharma / Lauren Bishop / Vivek Kulkarni) when:**
- The customer requires product guarantees (feature availability by date, “must-have” controls not currently offered).

---

## Evidence requests (SOC 2 / pen test / policies)
**Approved response (copy/paste):**
Redwood can provide security and compliance evidence (e.g., SOC 2 Type II report and/or pen test summary) under appropriate confidentiality terms. Please share the specific artifacts requested and we will follow our evidence-sharing process.

**Operational note (internal):** Do **not** attach restricted artifacts directly from personal email. Follow the internal evidence-sharing SOP.

**Pointer:** See “Customer Security Review Process” (restricted) for NDA requirements, approved distribution channels, and tracking.

---

## Approved answers by category

### 1) Compliance program / SOC 2
**Common prompts**
- “Do you have SOC 2? Provide report.”
- “What is the scope and period covered?”

**Base Answer (approved):**
Redwood maintains a formal security and compliance program. We can provide third-party assurance documentation (e.g., SOC 2 Type II) through our evidence-sharing process under appropriate confidentiality terms.

**Hosted / Dedicated / Private variants:**
- **Hosted:** SOC 2 scope includes controls operated by Redwood for the hosted service environment.
- **Dedicated:** Dedicated is operated by Redwood and follows the same core security program, with customer isolation at the capacity layer.
- **Private:** For Private deployments, responsibilities are shared; Redwood can provide assurance for Redwood-operated components and processes, while customer-managed infrastructure and surrounding controls may fall under the customer’s compliance scope.

**Evidence pointer:** SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA via GRC.

**Route to GRC when:** report, bridge letter, scope letter, or auditor contact is requested.

---

### 2) Data use / model training
**Common prompts**
- “Do you train models on our data?”
- “Is customer data used to improve models?”

**Base Answer (approved):**
Redwood processes customer inputs and outputs to provide the requested inference service. Customer content is not used to train Redwood-owned foundation models by default. Any use of customer data beyond service delivery would be governed by customer agreement and applicable configuration.

**Hosted / Dedicated / Private variants:**
- **Hosted:** Requests are processed within the hosted service boundary; operational metadata may be collected for service reliability and security monitoring.
- **Dedicated:** Data is processed within dedicated customer-isolated capacity.
- **Private:** Data processing occurs within the customer’s private environment boundary; telemetry and logging are configurable based on deployment architecture and customer requirements.

**Route to Legal when:** customer requests “no telemetry whatsoever” as a contractual guarantee, or requests custom data processing terms.

---

### 3) Encryption in transit
**Common prompts**
- “Is data encrypted in transit? Which protocols?”

**Base Answer (approved):**
Data in transit is encrypted using industry-standard protocols (e.g., TLS) for communications between clients and Redwood endpoints and for service-to-service communications within the platform, consistent with our security architecture.

**Hosted / Dedicated / Private variants:**
- **Hosted:** TLS is used for API access; internal service communications are protected per platform standards.
- **Dedicated:** Same approach as Hosted, with dedicated capacity.
- **Private:** Customer-controlled networking is part of the boundary; Redwood supports secure transport configurations suitable for private environments.

**Route to Security Eng when:** the customer requests specific cipher suites, mTLS requirements, or custom network security controls.

---

### 4) Encryption at rest + key management
**Common prompts**
- “Is data encrypted at rest? Do you support BYOK / KMS / HSM?”

**Base Answer (approved):**
Redwood uses encryption at rest for applicable systems storing customer data and service metadata, using standard cryptographic controls and managed key services where appropriate. Key management options depend on deployment mode and customer requirements.

**Hosted / Dedicated / Private variants:**
- **Hosted:** Encryption at rest is implemented within Redwood-managed cloud environments using managed key infrastructure.
- **Dedicated:** Same core approach as Hosted, applied to customer-isolated capacity.
- **Private:** Private deployments can integrate with customer-managed key management solutions (e.g., KMS/HSM) depending on architecture and deployment requirements.

**Route to Security Eng + Legal when:** customer requires contractual commitments around key custody, BYOK specifics, or escrow.

---

### 5) Identity, SSO (SAML), SCIM, MFA
**Common prompts**
- “Do you support SSO? SAML? MFA? SCIM provisioning?”

**Base Answer (approved):**
Redwood supports enterprise authentication and access controls to manage administrative access to the platform, including SSO options and role-based access control. Details depend on the customer’s deployment mode and identity architecture.

**Hosted / Dedicated / Private variants:**
- **Hosted:** SSO (SAML) is supported for Redwood Console access; administrative authentication policies can be enforced for enterprise tenants.
- **Dedicated:** Same Console and admin access patterns as Hosted.
- **Private:** Identity integration is supported; the exact integration pattern may vary based on Private deployment topology and customer identity requirements.

**Evidence pointer:** See “SSO (SAML) and SCIM One-Pager” and RBAC references.

**Route to Security Eng when:** customer requires non-standard IdP flows, conditional access requirements, or custom federation patterns.

---

### 6) RBAC / least privilege
**Common prompts**
- “Describe roles and permissions.”
- “Can you enforce least privilege? Is it auditable?”

**Base Answer (approved):**
Redwood provides role-based access control (RBAC) to support least-privilege access management. Administrative actions are auditable via platform logging.

**Hosted / Dedicated / Private variants:**
- **Hosted:** RBAC applies to Redwood Console and relevant administrative controls for the hosted tenant.
- **Dedicated:** RBAC applies similarly; dedicated capacity does not reduce the need for least-privilege controls.
- **Private:** RBAC applies to Redwood-managed components and administrative interfaces; customers may also enforce additional access controls in their environment.

**Evidence pointer:** “RBAC Model Reference” for the roles/permissions matrix.

---

### 7) Audit logging (admin + platform events)
**Common prompts**
- “Do you provide audit logs? What events are captured? Can we export to SIEM?”

**Base Answer (approved):**
Redwood provides audit logging for administrative and security-relevant activities within the platform. Audit log availability, event coverage, and export mechanisms can vary by deployment mode and customer configuration.

**Hosted / Dedicated / Private variants:**
- **Hosted:** Audit logs are available for key tenant/admin actions in the Redwood Console and can be accessed according to platform capabilities.
- **Dedicated:** Same audit logging approach as Hosted, with dedicated capacity.
- **Private:** Audit logging can be integrated with customer logging pipelines depending on deployment architecture; customers may also capture additional infrastructure-level logs within their environment.

**Evidence pointer:** “Audit Logging Overview One-Pager.”

**Route to Security Eng when:** customer requests a sample event payload, full schema export, retention customization, or SIEM integration specifics.

**Approved limitation phrasing (use as needed):**
Certain low-level infrastructure events may be available through underlying cloud or customer-managed logging rather than Redwood application audit logs, depending on deployment mode.

---

### 8) Logging, monitoring, and telemetry (non-audit)
**Common prompts**
- “What operational logs do you collect? Do logs contain customer data?”

**Base Answer (approved):**
Redwood collects logs and telemetry necessary to operate, secure, and improve reliability of the service (e.g., performance metrics, error logs). Logging is designed to minimize sensitive content exposure and is governed by access controls and retention policies.

**Hosted / Dedicated / Private variants:**
- **Hosted:** Redwood operates monitoring and logging for hosted environments.
- **Dedicated:** Same approach, with customer isolation at the capacity layer.
- **Private:** Logging/telemetry patterns are deployment-specific; customers may manage more of the monitoring stack, and telemetry configuration may vary.

**Route to Security Eng when:** customer requests guarantees about zero content in logs or requires custom logging filters.

---

### 9) Data retention and deletion
**Common prompts**
- “How long do you retain data? Can we request deletion? Is it configurable?”

**Base Answer (approved):**
Redwood retention practices vary by data type (e.g., customer content, audit logs, operational logs) and deployment mode. Redwood supports deletion requests in accordance with contractual requirements and applicable law. Some retention settings may be configurable depending on product and deployment.

**Hosted / Dedicated / Private variants:**
- **Hosted:** Retention defaults apply to hosted tenants; deletion requests are handled through standard support and compliance processes.
- **Dedicated:** Similar to Hosted; some controls may be tailored under enterprise agreements.
- **Private:** Customers may control retention for customer-managed components; Redwood provides guidance for Redwood-operated components based on deployment.

**Evidence pointer:** “Data Retention Controls One-Pager.”

**Route to GRC + Legal when:** the questionnaire requires a contractual retention guarantee, or references specific regulatory regimes requiring special handling.

---

### 10) Data residency / data location
**Common prompts**
- “Can you guarantee EU-only processing? Where is data stored? What about support access?”

**Base Answer (approved):**
Redwood supports regional deployments and can provide information about service regions and data flows. Data residency capabilities depend on deployment mode and selected region(s).

**Hosted / Dedicated / Private variants:**
- **Hosted:** Customer requests are processed in the selected service region(s) subject to platform availability.
- **Dedicated:** Dedicated capacity can be provisioned in supported regions, subject to availability.
- **Private:** Private deployments can be designed to meet specific residency requirements as the customer controls the environment boundary.

**Evidence pointer:** “Data Residency One-Pager.”

**Approved support-access phrasing:**
Support access is controlled and logged. Any access is performed on a least-privilege basis and consistent with support policies and contractual commitments.

**Route to Legal when:** customer requests a contractual “EU-only” guarantee, restrictions on remote access, or DPA amendments.

---

### 11) Subprocessors / third parties
**Common prompts**
- “List subprocessors. Do you notify us of changes?”

**Base Answer (approved):**
Redwood uses third-party service providers to support service delivery (e.g., infrastructure, monitoring, customer support tooling). Subprocessor disclosures and notification commitments (if any) are governed by the customer agreement and applicable data protection terms.

**Hosted / Dedicated / Private variants:**
- **Hosted/Dedicated:** Subprocessors may include cloud and operational tooling providers used to deliver and support the service.
- **Private:** The set of subprocessors may differ depending on deployment architecture; customers may also use their own vendors within their environment.

**Route to Legal when:** customer requests contractual subprocessor notice periods, audit rights for subprocessors, or custom subprocessor restrictions.

---

### 12) Vulnerability management + remediation SLAs
**Common prompts**
- “Do you scan for vulnerabilities? How quickly do you patch?”

**Base Answer (approved):**
Redwood maintains a vulnerability management program that includes regular scanning and remediation processes. Remediation prioritization is risk-based and considers severity, exploitability, and exposure.

**Hosted / Dedicated / Private variants:**
- **Hosted/Dedicated:** Redwood is responsible for patching Redwood-managed components.
- **Private:** Responsibilities are shared; Redwood provides guidance for Redwood components and customers manage patching for customer-managed infrastructure as applicable.

**Evidence pointer:** “Secure Development Lifecycle Summary.”

**Route to Security Eng when:** the customer asks for exact patch timelines or requests an exception-based SLA not already documented.

---

### 13) Penetration testing
**Common prompts**
- “Do you do pen tests? Can we see results? Can we pen test your service?”

**Base Answer (approved):**
Redwood conducts third-party security testing, which may include penetration testing, and can provide a pen test summary or relevant assurance documentation through the evidence-sharing process under appropriate confidentiality terms.

**Customer-initiated testing (approved):**
Customer-initiated penetration testing must be coordinated in advance and is subject to written authorization and scope controls.

**Route to GRC + Security Eng when:** the customer requests reports, wants to schedule a test, or requests a custom testing window.

---

### 14) Incident response + customer notification
**Common prompts**
- “What is your breach notification timeline?”
- “Do you notify within 24/48/72 hours?”

**Base Answer (approved):**
Redwood maintains an incident response program for security events, including processes for detection, triage, containment, eradication, recovery, and communication. Customer notification terms (including timing) are governed by the applicable agreement and the nature of the incident.

**Approved wording for timelines (use exactly):**
Redwood will provide notification consistent with contractual commitments and applicable law. Specific notification timelines, where applicable, are addressed in the customer agreement.

**Evidence pointer:** “Incident Response and Notification One-Pager.”

**Route to Legal immediately when:** the customer demands a specific notification window (e.g., “within 24 hours”) in the questionnaire or contract.

---

### 15) Business continuity / disaster recovery
**Common prompts**
- “Do you have BCP/DR? RTO/RPO?”

**Base Answer (approved):**
Redwood maintains business continuity and disaster recovery practices appropriate to the services offered. Detailed recovery objectives may depend on deployment mode and customer contract.

**Hosted / Dedicated / Private variants:**
- **Hosted/Dedicated:** Redwood manages availability and recovery practices for the service environment.
- **Private:** Responsibility is shared; customer infrastructure design and operational procedures may materially affect recovery outcomes.

**Route to Security Eng + Legal when:** the customer requests exact RTO/RPO values as contractual commitments.

---

### 16) Access controls (internal access, support, and production)
**Common prompts**
- “Who can access production? Is access logged? Background checks?”

**Base Answer (approved):**
Redwood limits internal access to production systems based on least privilege and job role, and administrative access is logged. Redwood uses controlled access processes for sensitive environments.

**Hosted / Dedicated / Private variants:**
- **Hosted/Dedicated:** Redwood controls access to Redwood-managed environments.
- **Private:** Customer controls access to customer-managed components and may further restrict Redwood support access based on deployment architecture and agreement.

**Route to GRC when:** the customer requests HR policy evidence, background check details, or formal policy documents.

---

### 17) Secure SDLC / change management
**Common prompts**
- “Do you perform code reviews? Security testing? Change approvals?”

**Base Answer (approved):**
Redwood follows a secure software development lifecycle, including peer review, automated testing, and security controls integrated into development and release workflows.

**Evidence pointer:** “Secure Development Lifecycle Summary.”

---

### 18) Data privacy / DPA
**Common prompts**
- “Will you sign a DPA? GDPR/CCPA?”

**Base Answer (approved):**
Redwood supports data protection and privacy requirements through contractual terms (including DPAs where applicable) and operational controls appropriate to the service.

**Route to Legal when:** the customer requests a DPA, SCCs, or privacy addendum language.

---

## “Where to find it” (field packaging)
Use these to send customer-safe materials quickly.

**Customer-safe (can be shared by Sales/SE):**
- Security FAQ v2 (PDF) — field-ready
- One-pagers pack (PDF): Data Residency, Data Retention Controls, Audit Logging Overview, SSO/SAML & SCIM, Secure SDLC, Incident Response & Notification

**Restricted (GRC-controlled distribution under NDA):**
- SOC 2 Type II report (full)
- Pen test report / detailed findings (if requested)
- Policy documents (as applicable)

---

## Approved “roadmap” phrasing (copy/paste)
When asked for future features or timing:
We continuously improve our security and compliance program. We can share our current capabilities and discuss potential enhancements, but we do not commit to specific future features or timelines in questionnaires. Any commitments, if applicable, must be documented in the customer agreement.

---

## Redlines to avoid (common pitfalls)
Do not use these phrases in RFP responses:
- “We guarantee 100% uptime”
- “We never store any customer data”
- “We will notify within 24 hours” (unless Legal has approved in the contract)
- “We are compliant with [framework]” when the framework is not formally attested/certified

If a prospect insists on these, route to **Legal** and/or **GRC**.

---

## Ownership, review cadence, and change requests
**Owner:** Security & Compliance PM (Naomi Feldman)

**Approvers (required):**
- Security Engineering (Marcus Lin)
- GRC/Compliance (Olga Petrov)
- Legal (Michael Grant) for contractual or legally-sensitive claims
- Solutions Engineering review (Markus Klein) for field usability

**Review cadence:** Quarterly, and anytime there is a material change to:
- Deployment modes or security boundary
- Audit log coverage/export mechanisms
- Retention/residency defaults
- Compliance attestations

**Change request intake:** Use the “Security Appendix Requests Intake” process for tracked redlines and approvals.

---

## Quick copy/paste snippets (short-form)
Use these for tight form fields.

**Encryption (short):**
Data is encrypted in transit using TLS and encrypted at rest using standard cryptographic controls; key management options vary by deployment mode.

**Audit logs (short):**
Redwood provides audit logging for administrative/security-relevant activity; coverage and export options vary by deployment mode.

**SOC 2 (short):**
Redwood can provide SOC 2 Type II assurance documentation under NDA via our evidence-sharing process.

**Incident notification (short):**
Redwood maintains an incident response program and provides customer notification consistent with contractual commitments and applicable law.
